title: A good quarter with one category quietly falling over
variant: Six small multiples on one scale, and the total hides all of it
prompt: Put together the quarterly numbers for the shop. Takings are up but something feels off about children's.
note: The cover, and the clearest case for small multiples: six categories on one shared scale, where children's has halved over a year and fiction grew by almost exactly what children's lost, so the total says nothing happened. Two Plot traps are visible in the source and worth copying -- the x domain is written out because a band scale would otherwise order 'Q4 24' through 'Q3 26' alphabetically and draw the line as a zigzag, and the last-quarter dots are filtered through the mark's own `filter` rather than by handing it a shorter array, which inside a facet would put them in the wrong panels. The basket histogram exists to make the same point twice: the average basket is £13.18 and almost nobody spends £13.
